slides.title: Inheritance & Polymorphism Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers base and derived classes, modes of inheritance, virtual functions, method overriding, abstract classes, pure virtual functions, and vtables (CPP_209 to CPP_216).

slides.title: Inheritance Syntax (CPP_209)
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol used to declare that a derived class inherits from a base class.

slides.title: Protected Access Specifier (CPP_210)
slides.prompt: Which statement correctly describes 'protected' members of a base class?
options: Accessible within the base class and its derived classes, but hidden from outside code
Accessible everywhere in the program without restrictions
Accessible only inside the base class and hidden from derived classes
Accessible only by static functions in external files
slides.correctAnswer: Accessible within the base class and its derived classes, but hidden from outside code

slides.title: Public Inheritance Access (CPP_210)
slides.prompt: Fill in the access keyword so public members of the base class remain public in the derived class.

slides.title: Virtual Functions (CPP_211)
slides.prompt: Why do we declare a base class member function as 'virtual' in C++?
options: To enable runtime dynamic binding (polymorphism) when called through base pointers
To make the function execute faster during compile-time
To prevent derived classes from overriding it
To allow the function to be called without creating an object instance
slides.correctAnswer: To enable runtime dynamic binding (polymorphism) when called through base pointers

slides.title: Virtual Keyword (CPP_211)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to allow dynamic dispatch for a base class method.

slides.title: Pure Virtual Functions (CPP_212)
slides.prompt: What syntax is used to declare a Pure Virtual Function in a base class?

slides.title: Pure Virtual Assignment (CPP_212)
slides.prompt: Fill in the assignment value that turns a virtual function into a pure virtual function.

slides.title: Abstract Classes (CPP_213)
slides.prompt: Which of the following is true regarding Abstract Classes in C++?
options: You cannot instantiate an object directly from an abstract class
An abstract class cannot contain constructors
All member variables in an abstract class must be static
Abstract classes cannot have derived subclasses
slides.correctAnswer: You cannot instantiate an object directly from an abstract class

slides.title: Override Specifier (CPP_214)
slides.prompt: Fill in the modern C++ (C++11) specifier used to ensure a derived method correctly overrides a base virtual method.

slides.title: Virtual Destructors (CPP_215)
slides.prompt: Why should a base class with virtual functions always have a 'virtual destructor'?
options: To guarantee that derived class destructors are called when deleting via base pointers
To prevent derived classes from destroying base class memory
To allow private member cleanup automatically
slides.correctAnswer: To guarantee that derived class destructors are called when deleting via base pointers

slides.title: Final Specifier (CPP_214)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword that prevents further overriding of a virtual function in derived classes.

slides.title: Diamond Problem & Virtual Inheritance (CPP_216)
slides.prompt: How does C++ resolve the 'Diamond Problem' in multiple inheritance?
options: By using virtual base classes (virtual inheritance)
By converting all classes into static classes
By overriding destructor calls in base classes
slides.correctAnswer: By using virtual base classes (virtual inheritance)
